ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, connect OE, intersecting CD at point F,\\
$\because$ from (1) we know that quadrilateral OCED is a rhombus,\\
$\therefore$ OE $\perp$ CD,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC=\angle OFC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ AD $\parallel$ OE,\\
$\because$ DE $\parallel$ AC,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral AOED is a parallelogram,\\
$\therefore$ OE=AD=BC=$\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, with $DE \parallel AC$ and $CE \parallel BD$. Quadrilateral $ODEC$ is a rhombus; connect $OE$. If $BC = 2\sqrt{2}$, find the length of $OE$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, connect OE, intersecting CD at point F,\\ $\because$ from (1) we know that quadrilateral OCED is a rhombus,\\ $\therefore$ OE $\perp$ CD,\\ $\therefore \angle ADC=\angle OFC=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ AD $\parallel$ OE,\\ $\because$ DE $\parallel$ AC,\\ $\therefore$ quadrilateral AOED is a parallelogram,\\ $\therefore$ OE=AD=BC=$\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$

Image description: In the figure is a rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, D is at the upper right, C is at the lower right; the diagonals AC and BD of the rectangle intersect at O. Point E is on the right side of CD, connect DE, CE, and OE is also drawn in the figure. The figure shows that O-D-E-C forms a rhombus, and OE intersects CD.

Reasoning: Because quadrilateral ODEC is a rhombus, its two diagonals OE and DC are perpendicular to each other, that is, OE ⟂ DC. In rectangle ABCD, AD ⟂ DC, therefore OE ∥ AD. Also because the given condition DE ∥ AC, and A, O, C are on the same straight line, so DE ∥ AO. Thus in quadrilateral AOED, AO ∥ DE, AD ∥ OE, two pairs of opposite sides are respectively parallel, therefore AOED is a parallelogram. So OE = AD. The opposite sides of rectangle ABCD are equal, AD = BC. It is known that BC = 2√2, therefore OE = 2√2.
